Jackboots in the House Parliament

By: Joy Summers | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
The chaotic scenes in Parliament shocked South Africa now that calm has been restored many questions remain

Further information:
Jackboots in the house
Some called it the death of the Rainbow nation – Last week, parliament descended into chaos. Within the first hour the speaker Baleka Mbete lost control of the house. It was only restored when ANC Stone Sizane agreed with the opposition that they should stick to the agreed proceedings for the day. But as the ANC tried to push through the Ad Hoc Committee’s report on Nkandla, it was clear that the opposition were united despite race and ideology. For hours the opposition embarked on a strategy of filibustering – frustrating the ruling party and infuriating an imperious Baleka Mbete. But more was to come – hours later during the debate on the Grand Inga Hydro Electric scheme when most journalists had left the house the EFF Reneiloe Mashabela in her address called President Zuma ‘the greatest thief in the world’ and refused to withdraw her comments. Cedrick Frolich called the seargent at arms to remove her and when parliaments own security decided not to enter the house – riot police stormed the national assembly roughing up opposition MP’s – but only a small cell phone from the gallery recorded the fracas as someone pulled the live parliamentary feed.
What happened last week shocked a nation. Business Day Editor and founder of the Midrand Group – a think tank largely made up of black intellectuals – Songezo Zibi was grim in his assessment: “ We are in blind denial about how bad it is going to get. The rot shall continue unabated, in Parliament and elsewhere, “ he said.
But what did it all mean – for political analyst Stephen Grootes the ANC despite their majority are bewildered. As Cosatu disintegrates the ruling party now find themselves fighting a war on two fronts. And if we are looking for an answer on how the ANC will deal with losing power, their jackboots tactics in Parliament gave a hint at that- not well! According to other analysts.
By Tuesday Deputy President Cyril Ramaphosa had done what he does best- bring warring groups together and find a way forward. Using his considerable skills gained at Codesa, he managed to pull off what Nic Borain called a miracle. At a photo opportunity outside Tuinhuis the opposition parliamentary leaders agreed to a a range of interventions to restore calm and dignity to the house.
But said the DA Mmusi Maimane that agreement did not preclude further robust debate. There are only days left before this 5th Parliament is adjourned for the year. But many questions remain despite the truce –is our democracy in danger as some suggest and what of the damage incurred to our international image.

Joy viewing: Parliament
Duncan George Amalia Nan joy
21/11/2014 04:24:59 PM

1. Change first shot of Zuma doesn’t look dignified at all – places us semiotically in opposition to Zuma. Use him looking presidential give him the dignity of his office.
2. It is confusing when we come to Litchfield Shabalala – did she meet Zuma and tell him what she is saying herself.
3. We need to indicate when the events we are seeing in parliament actually happened as its confusing...
4. Be clear about which parts of what we have seen in parliament the commentators are talking about
5. Bongani’s link about police storming twice and South Africans asking what is going on needs to come at the beginning or we don’t need it. All you need in its place is an exterior shot of parliament – the turmoil in the house might appear to go on behind closed doors but what goes on behind those doors spills over into society.
6. Rather than boiling frogs you need to say like frogs in boiling water
7. You haven’t represented the ANC’s arguments enough... Matole Motshega you need to give him some platform time. Cyril is not representing the ANC
8. The story isn’t balanced without the ANC add in quite a lot.
9. Would help to put Songezo in earlier. AND bring in his comment about the last 10 years and precede the boiling frog comment with that.
10. Can you add in something about why this is problematic to the country and economy...
11. As much as possible zoom in past the sign language translator and where not possible split the screen in places etc
12. Take out the pictures of Musi Maimane over his interview.

Press Release:


Parly Politics
There’s nothing unusual about heated debate and the odd scathing remark in Parliament. But when riot police are called in to forcefully restore order to the House and eyewitness accounts paint a picture of tussles in the passages, are we still seeing a robust democracy at work? Carte Blanche investigates Parliament’s descent into chaos and asks what this means for our young democracy.


Script:


Jackboots final script TX 23rd November

Commentary One
Parliament, Thursday 13th November began with a prayer, / but within 15 minutes- replaced by a cacophony

…And we are not going to stand for it
Take your seat
I will not!
NO …Leave the house …
Its abuse of Power!

Commentary Two
This was the day the house was scheduled to debate the Ad hoc committee’s Nkandla report. Unable to stop the adoption of its findings, the opposition chose instead, to delay it. It was a day of filibustering, howlers and insults, and a day that the opposition united across ideology against the ANC

Mmusi Maimane
Today the opposition stands together united in rejection of this report in its rejection of its denials, half- truths and fallacies

Motshekga
Today honorable Maimane sank into the pigsty of dirty politics, he rejected the report without a factual, legal and constitutional basis

Commentary three evidence/ off the grid / use agitation at 01 18
Seven months ago President Zuma weathered the Nkandla storm, presiding over a respectable 62% win in the May election. But in August, question time brought its own humiliation.

Julius Malema
I have only one question for you – when are you going to pay back the money?
President Zuma: I did pay back the money
EFF chanting: Pay back the money, pay back the money
Commentary Four off the grid
Since that day, President Zuma has refused to return to the National assembly to answer questions. Pay back the money day also cost 12 EFF MP’s a possible suspension. Khanyisile Litchfield-TShabalala is an EFF MP.
Kanyisile Litchfield Shabalala: The president wants assurances that what happened in August wont happen again. You must make a commitment that you will answer, because if you aren’t going to answer you yourself are responsible if the house collapses – its like you are here but you are not, because you are not answering.

Commentary five under pressure
As the 13th November dragged on into the night- MP’s slugged it out.

Mathole Motshekga
In South Africa there is no constitutional crisis, there is a constitutional illiteracy on the part of the DA led unholy political alliance…

Commentary six
When the EFF’s Reneilwe Mashabela addressed the house, she set in motion a chain of events that have rippled throughout this week and into the next

Reneilwe Mashabela
The president is the greatest thief in the world and I wont withdraw!

Commentary seven burned earth may be too big/ under pressure use radio glitch
In came police in riot gear, who had been on standby in a nearby office. The DA stormed the police at the door- some MP’s were injured, and cabinet minister Lindiwe Zulu had to be restrained in the passages. / But only a handful of images captured the shame because someone cut the live feed

Commentary eight - again radio glitch
EWN’s political analyst, Stephen Grootes has been in the gallery this week

Stephen
What happened in parliament is abhorrent to watch, you certainly wouldn’t want your children to behave like that, at the same time it’s the opposition flexing its muscles for the first time and so we see our politics …the anc is facing a cost for decisions that it has made, that is how democracies are supposed to work, that is not a bad thing in the long run.
Link: Its been a field day for journo’s, analysts and commentators with some even suggesting that we are at the edge of a precipice, but we have weathered many storms before and are a resilient people – but that is precisely the problem says Songezo Zibi
Commentary nine analyse / approaching the hour
We have got used to a lack of accountability says the Business day editor.
Songezo
What we see in parliament is an accountability system, a political system that is no longer able to respond adequately to the very serious problems of political decay and the collapse of governance in the country
Commentary ten: He has said he is reminded of frogs in a boiling pot

Songezo
The frog is not dead yet and the water isn’t boiling yet but it is getting somewhere and we need to change the picture

Commentary eleven
On Monday he wrote: “The rot shall continue unabated in parliament and elsewhere

Songezo
So it is not the last time it is going to happen again – you can hold me to that – so we have seen scenes that we have not seen before – lets take it outside …ten years ago…you would …and cops we are now used to this stage of dysfunction the question is what is next?

Commentary Twelve
It’s been a tough few days for Baleka Mbete, after she lost control of the house on the 13th November

Up sound
Baleka ….I was standing first

Commentary Thirteen
And MP’s accused her of bias.

She must go she must go

LINK
Baleka must go say the opposition but it doesn’t look she is going anywhere

Songezo
A lot of people blame the speaker – I don’t – the fundamental problem is that we have a massive public expenditure scandal on our hands– the fracas is a rebellion against the powerlessness of the opposition …that is why a lot of people are saying I enjoy what is happening in parliament because for the first time the ANC is but there is a danger they are in because a dysfunctional parliament serves no one

Commentary Sixteen
Protecting our institutions is imperative says Mmusi Maimane- parliamentary leader of the DA, thrust into the job 7 months ago
Mmusi Maimane : It is a daunting task because when all alse fails this institution must stand, and If I do anything with my own life it is to say I will spend my life at least fighting for that because when that is in place it doesn’t matter whether another President Zuma or anyone elses rises up we can always know that we can bequeath to our future generations that at least the constitutions still stand at least the institutions will still stand


Commentary eighteen
Restoring dignity to parliament fell to Deputy President Cyril Ramaphosa on Tuesday at Tuyhuis. He spent the morning of his birthday doing what Cyril does best – creating peace from conflict.

Cyril
We have a sense that parliament was having a crisis – that we needed to address collectively

Commentary nineteen
Amongst others the meeting agreed that the rules should be applied fairly without fear, favour or prejudice, to reject any attempt to suppress debate or silence dissent, and to hold in abeyance the disciplining of EFF members

ANC chief whip Stone Sizane and DA Mmusi Maimane would work together under the Deputy President

Cyril Ramaphosa
With a view of restoring its dignity, its integrity and its standing in the eyes of our people…

Up sound Mmusi Maimane
Vote to censor the president

Commentary Twenty
But a day later the truce collapsed when the DA proposed a motion of censure against President Zuma for his failure to appear in the house to answer oral questions./ In our interview with Songezo Zibi only a few hours beforehand he predicted exactly that

Songezo
It’s a temporary truce – the whole thing will fall apart again that is at the heart of the dysfunction in parliament there was a question that required an answer in Parliament and the answer was not given

Commentary Twenty- One
With the deal in tatters, the DA protested outside of parliament on Thursday, each placard representing what they believed were unanswered or unsatisfactorily answered questions

Up sound
Where is president Zuma?

Helen Zille at protest
There are many hundreds of questions that have gone unanswered ….and that undermines the spirit of accountability and THAT is the heart of our constitution



Commentary Twenty- two
The president won’t return to parliament this year. Cyril Ramaphosa will have to use his considerable skills to bring the warring parties back to a truce next week. This week ended in disgrace

Up sound Lechesa Tsenoli
Honorable members you are a disgrace and it is despicable the way you are behaving

Commentary Twenty-Three
Meanwhile questions go unanswered

Songezo Zibi
We haven’t had substantive answers from this executive for a long time and this parliament has been unwilling and unable to extract the kind of answers that are required and that is why I have said before and I will say it again Parliament as we have it now is ineffective and a monumental waste of money

THE END 10 min 10 sec

metadata.Further information: Jackboots in the house Some called it the death of the Rainbow nation – Last week, parliament descended into chaos. Within the first hour the speaker Baleka Mbete lost control of the house. It was only restored when ANC Stone Sizane agreed with the opposition that they should stick to the agreed proceedings for the day. But as the ANC tried to push through the Ad Hoc Committee’s report on Nkandla, it was clear that the opposition were united despite race and ideology. For hours the opposition embarked on a strategy of filibustering – frustrating the ruling party and infuriating an imperious Baleka Mbete. But more was to come – hours later during the debate on the Grand Inga Hydro Electric scheme when most journalists had left the house the EFF Reneiloe Mashabela in her address called President Zuma ‘the greatest thief in the world’ and refused to withdraw her comments. Cedrick Frolich called the seargent at arms to remove her and when parliaments own security decided not to enter the house – riot police stormed the national assembly roughing up opposition MP’s – but only a small cell phone from the gallery recorded the fracas as someone pulled the live parliamentary feed. What happened last week shocked a nation. Business Day Editor and founder of the Midrand Group – a think tank largely made up of black intellectuals – Songezo Zibi was grim in his assessment: “ We are in blind denial about how bad it is going to get. The rot shall continue unabated, in Parliament and elsewhere, “ he said. But what did it all mean – for political analyst Stephen Grootes the ANC despite their majority are bewildered. As Cosatu disintegrates the ruling party now find themselves fighting a war on two fronts. And if we are looking for an answer on how the ANC will deal with losing power, their jackboots tactics in Parliament gave a hint at that- not well! According to other analysts. By Tuesday Deputy President Cyril Ramaphosa had done what he does best- bring warring groups together and find a way forward. Using his considerable skills gained at Codesa, he managed to pull off what Nic Borain called a miracle. At a photo opportunity outside Tuinhuis the opposition parliamentary leaders agreed to a a range of interventions to restore calm and dignity to the house. But said the DA Mmusi Maimane that agreement did not preclude further robust debate. There are only days left before this 5th Parliament is adjourned for the year. But many questions remain despite the truce –is our democracy in danger as some suggest and what of the damage incurred to our international image.

metadata.Viewing Notes: Joy viewing: Parliament Duncan George Amalia Nan joy 21/11/2014 04:24:59 PM 1. Change first shot of Zuma doesn’t look dignified at all – places us semiotically in opposition to Zuma. Use him looking presidential give him the dignity of his office. 2. It is confusing when we come to Litchfield Shabalala – did she meet Zuma and tell him what she is saying herself. 3. We need to indicate when the events we are seeing in parliament actually happened as its confusing... 4. Be clear about which parts of what we have seen in parliament the commentators are talking about 5. Bongani’s link about police storming twice and South Africans asking what is going on needs to come at the beginning or we don’t need it. All you need in its place is an exterior shot of parliament – the turmoil in the house might appear to go on behind closed doors but what goes on behind those doors spills over into society. 6. Rather than boiling frogs you need to say like frogs in boiling water 7. You haven’t represented the ANC’s arguments enough... Matole Motshega you need to give him some platform time. Cyril is not representing the ANC 8. The story isn’t balanced without the ANC add in quite a lot. 9. Would help to put Songezo in earlier. AND bring in his comment about the last 10 years and precede the boiling frog comment with that. 10. Can you add in something about why this is problematic to the country and economy... 11. As much as possible zoom in past the sign language translator and where not possible split the screen in places etc 12. Take out the pictures of Musi Maimane over his interview.
